entries.title: I John 3:1
segments:
The Father. These words include in their meaning not only 'My Father,' as rightfully spoken in a special sense by Jesus Christ alone, but 'our Father' of the Lord's Prayer.
 

 
 World. The evil in the world.  See note on 1Jo 2.15.  In this and the first six verses of the succeeding chapter the main theme is the righteousness of God.

entries.title: I John 3:2
segments: What we shall be. Children of God, however blessed their condition, are privileged to reach still greater spiritual heights.  This is also clearly indicated by Paul, whose use of the words 'sons of God' (Ro 8.14) implies a matured consciousness of the filial relation impossible to children under tutelage. 'Sons of God' rejoice in the liberty and glory conferred upon them.  There is no limit to their spiritual attainment except perfect conformity to the image of the Son of God (

entries.title: I John 3:3
segments:
This hope. Of becoming like God by following the example of Christ.
 

 
 Set on him. Given to him or conferred on him. Man depends upon God even for the hope of becoming like Him.

entries.title: I John 3:4
segments: Sin is lawlessness. Because it prevents obedience to God.

entries.title: I John 3:6
segments:
Sinneth not. That is, not and cannot be an habitual, confirmed sinner.  If any man professing to abide in Christ commit sin, to that extent he does not abide in him.
 

 
 Hath not seen him, neither knoweth him. Because sin is out of all harmony with him.  See notes on

entries.title: I John 3:7
segments: Even as he. Christ.

entries.title: I John 3:8
segments:
Doeth sin. That is, sins habitually.
 

 
 Works of the devil. The sins into which mankind has been tempted.

entries.title: I John 3:9
segments:
Begotten of God. Whosoever has been made and remains a child of god.
 

 
 His seed abideth in him. The spiritual life in him grows, and becomes more active and fruitful.

entries.title: I John 3:10
segments: That loveth not his brother. Love for mankind, whether Christian believers or not, is the practical test of love to God.

entries.title: I John 3:12
segments: Cain. See

.
 

 
 Of the evil one. Inspired by the evil one.

entries.title: I John 3:14
segments: Out of death into life, because, etc.  Or, out of darkness into light (

entries.title: I John 3:15
segments: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Because murder begins, is planned and is done through hatred.  See
and note thereon.

entries.title: I John 3:16
segments: Brethren. All mankind, especially the children of God.

entries.title: I John 3:17
segments: Beholdeth. Looks on with indifference.

entries.title: I John 3:19
segments:
Hereby. That is, because we have loved in deed and in truth (1Jo 3.18).
 

 
 Assure our heart before him. Be comforted by trusting God for forgiveness.

entries.title: I John 3:20
segments: Greater than our heart. More merciful than we are when our consciences condemn us through imperfect knowledge. 'For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust' (

entries.title: I John 3:22
segments: Whatsoever we ask we receive. Prayer to God is answered at the moment of asking, according to faith, but not always in the manner asked or expected.  The answer may be known or seen in an instant, or it may be given through years of waiting, though in a way which makes clear the unwisdom of the first request and enhances the goodness of God.  See

and note thereon.
 

 
 Commandments. Obedience to God, which is not perfect so long as it contains any element of fear.  See note on

.
 

 
 Pleasing in his sight. Things done from love to God, a better motive than obedience strictly so called.  But love, like obedience, is imperfect so long as any fear lurks within the heart.  'He that feareth is not made perfect in love' (
).  If we are willing to hear God and to obey his voice, He will hear and grant our petition.

entries.title: I John 3:24
segments: The Spirit which he gave us. After accepting the rule of Christ in the heart.  The approval of the Spirit witnesses that God in Christ abides within us.
